Subject: Strategic data-layer partnership — cost & support alignment

Hi Aisha,

Great meeting last week — thanks for the time. Following up with a short proposal for how Pinecone and Redwood could structure a commercial + support partnership for Vector DB usage across your Dedicated and Private customers. High level:

- Joint enterprise offer: tiered discounts tied to committed query units and reserved index capacity.
- Technical support overlay: direct engineering on-call for the first 6 months of any co-sold account, plus expedited index rebuild SLOs for critical customers.
- Co-marketing/enablement: joint case study + joint webinar in Q3.

I've attached a cost model with a couple of scenarios (see attachment). Also flagged a couple of items we expect on legal side (data residency language and a short MSA addendum).

Attachment: pinecone_cost_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Proposed next steps: 1) quick internal alignment on Redwood asks; 2) 30-min call with Devon (alliances) + your engineering lead to map technical handoffs; 3) draft MSA addendum to share with your legal.

Would you be open to a kickoff call next week?

Cheers,
Oliver Hayes
Head of Strategic Alliances, Pinecone
oliver@pinecone.io

Thanks for the ping — quick thoughts:

1) Pilot structure: propose a 6-month pilot with 3 reference customers (one Hosted, one Dedicated, one Private) to validate performance & support handoffs. Success metrics: avg p99 latency under target, index rebuild time < X hrs, and cost per 10k queries.

2) Commercial asks: we can consider co-sell credits for the first 3 co-sold deals or a revenue share model. I prefer credits (simple to invoice) but want finance to sign off on the math.

3) Support model: Pinecone's offer for engineering on-call for the first 6 months is good, but we need clear escalation matrix and runbook ownership. Jonas, can your team define the minimal runbook steps Pinecone must follow?

4) Legal/Procurement: flagging that we will not accept open-ended indemnity. Marissa — can procurement draft a short addendum that covers: data residency, SOC2 evidence, indemnity cap, and SLA credit formulas?

I'll grab time for a 30-min alignment with Aisha and Jonas on Wed afternoon.

-karthik
VP, Partnerships & GTM

Looping in procurement/legal approach. Quick list of non-negotiables and asks from our side:

- Data residency: any customer data we route to Pinecone must obey customer's region selection; we need a written attestation for EU-resident customers.
- SOC2 / security evidence: request their latest Type II and pen-test summary.
- Indemnity & liability: propose mutual indemnification with a capped liability linked to the deal value; no open-ended clauses.
- SLA credits: define p99 and p95 targets + credits formula; require an initial 30-day remediation window before credits start.
- Procurement paperwork: we need the completed vendor questionnaire (I attached our standard template).

Attachment: vendor_questionnaire.pdf (form)

Please keep the scope of the MSA addendum tight. We should avoid embedding product-level SLAs in the MSA; instead, include them as an appendix the partner can update.

Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
